subject: DPA: transfer impact language, SCCs & UK IDTA addendum coordination
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nordtech.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nordtech.com
Date: 2026-05-16T11:02:00Z
Subject: Initial DPA redlines + transfer impact questions

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement has started the DPA review and attached our initial redlines (see file). Two specific items they flagged are:

- SCCs: they expect the EU SCCs to be executed (we assume via an addendum or in-doc SCC incorporation).
- UK transfers: they asked whether Redwood will sign the UK IDTA addendum or accept equivalent transfer language in the DPA.

Can you confirm whether Redwood prefers: (a) inline SCC incorporation in the DPA, (b) a separate SCC addendum, or (c) the UK IDTA as a separate executed addendum? They also want to see the current subprocessors list and a short transfer impact assessment that covers subprocessors outside the EEA/UK.

Copying procurement on next steps.

Regards,
Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Procurement, NordTech

Attachment: NordTech_DPA_Redlines_v1.docx (docx)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nordtech.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-17T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + transfer impact questions

Hi Liam — thanks for the redlines and the clear ask. Quick summary on our side:

- We typically incorporate the EU SCCs via an addendum that references the DPA; this keeps the DPA lean and makes versioning easier.
- For UK transfers, Redwood can sign the IDTA addendum (we've executed it in prior deals) OR include transfer-impact language in the DPA if the customer prefers a single document. The choice is mostly contractual preference rather than a blocker.
- Subprocessors: I'll attach the current certified subprocessors list (we refresh quarterly). For subprocessors outside EEA/UK we include standard additional safeguards; the transfer-impact assessment is short — we map subprocessors to risk categories and mitigation (MMAs, SCCs, contractual controls).

Next steps I propose:
1) I'll circulate our redline (v3) with the SCC addendum template attached.
2) Legal (Karthik) can propose a one-doc vs two-doc approach for NordTech.
3) If they prefer IDTA, we'll confirm signatory flow (DocuSign or AdobeSign) and timing.

Looping Marissa for procurement cadence and Karthik for legal sign-off.

Thanks,
Aditya
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Redline_v3.docx (docx); subprocessors_current_list_20260515.csv (csv)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T14:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial DPA redlines + transfer impact questions

Thanks — a few legal notes after a quick pass on the redline: 

1) SCCs vs inline: I recommend the separate SCC addendum approach. It simplifies later model/terms updates and maps cleanly to our SOPs. We'll attach the EU Module 2/Module 3 options depending on data types.

2) UK IDTA: we can execute the UK IDTA addendum for customers that require it. The only redline we request is clarifying Subprocessor notification timelines (we push for 10 days notice + mitigation window).

3) Transfer impact assessment: we should provide a concise one-pager that:
   - Lists subprocessors outside EEA/UK, jurisdiction, and legal basis for transfer (SCCs or adequacy).
   - Notes encryption and contractual safeguards in place, plus any reliance on risk exceptions.

4) Procurement-led redlines around liability caps and indemnities will need commercial sign-off (Marissa).

I'll prepare a legal-ready package (DPA + SCC addendum + IDTA optional addendum + transfer impact one-pager). If NordTech wants everything in one doc, we can produce that but prefer modular docs.

—Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Helen Frost <helen.frost@legalpart.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nordtech.com>, procurement@nordtech.com
Date: 2026-05-20T08:54:00Z
Subject: NordTech comments on Redwood redline

Team — thanks for the revised package. A couple of points from Legal at NordTech after reviewing Redwood_DPA_Redline_v3: 

- They prefer the UK IDTA as a separate executed addendum (they want an explicit signature block).
- They requested additional transfer-impact detail for subprocessors in India and Singapore: specifically whether Redwood intends to rely on SCCs for those transfers or another lawful basis.
- They asked that the subprocessor notification window be 14 days, not 10.

We can be flexible but procurement will push on the notification timeframe. If Redwood can agree to 14 days (or provide a backstop process to accelerate mitigations), it would smooth the path. Also please confirm whether Redwood is open to using DocuSign for the IDTA execution; procurement prefers DocuSign envelope flows that tie back to the main SOW.

Best,
Helen Frost
Counsel, LegalPart (external counsel to NordTech)

Attachment: NordTech_Comments_20260520.pdf (pdf)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@nordtech.com>, Helen Frost <helen.frost@legalpart.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-22T17:38:00Z
Subject: Re: NordTech comments on Redwood redline — proposed compromise

Hi Liam / Helen — appreciate the clarity. Proposal from Redwood to close the loop quickly: 

1) Execution mechanics: we'll agree to execute the UK IDTA as a separate addendum with its own signature block. DocuSign works for us; we'll create a single envelope that contains: (a) Master Services Agreement (if applicable), (b) DPA, and (c) IDTA addendum so procurement has a single envelope audit trail.

2) Notification window: we can accept a 14-day notification window for standard subprocessors. For high-impact subprocessors (classification will be in the transfer-impact one-pager) we'll commit to a 10-business-day accelerated review and provide a named escalation contact. That hybrid should address procurement's timeline concerns while preserving operational flexibility.

3) Transfer impact for India / SG: Redwood will mark each subprocessor with the transfer mechanism (EU SCCs, adequacy decision where applicable, or supplemental safeguards). For operators where SCCs apply, we'll indicate whether we host on a subprocessors' regional infrastructure or rely on our cross-border processing flows.

Action items I will take this week:
- Finalize the transfer-impact one-pager and attach to the DPA package.
- Prepare the DocuSign envelope and propose an execution timeline (target: complete signatures within 7 business days after approval).
- Marissa will confirm any commercial changes tied to liability language.

If that reads OK, please say "approved" in reply and we'll push the DocuSign envelope today.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
